# Horus community code of conduct

## Participation

Everyone participating in Horus Issues, Discussions, pull requests, or other
project-managed spaces is expected to help make them welcoming and useful.
This applies to maintainers and contributors alike, and when representing the
project publicly.

Treat people with respect regardless of experience, disability, age, appearance,
race, ethnicity, nationality, religion, gender identity, or sexual orientation.
Ask questions in good faith, explain technical disagreements, and accept
constructive feedback. Focus criticism on ideas and behavior. Give people room
to learn and correct mistakes; nobody owes you unpaid work or an immediate reply.

Harassment, threats, discriminatory language, sexual attention, personal attacks,
doxxing, sharing another person's private information without permission, spam,
and repeated disruption are unacceptable. Do not solicit credentials or post
private logs or code. Respect the same standards in replies and private contact
connected to project participation.

## Reporting a concern

For content or conduct that violates GitHub's rules, use GitHub's
[reporting tools](https://docs.github.com/en/communities/maintaining-your-safety-on-github/reporting-abuse-or-spam).
Reporting to GitHub goes to GitHub, not to the Horus maintainers.

For a project moderation concern that can safely be discussed publicly, leave a
brief request for maintainer attention in the relevant thread. Describe the
behavior and link the relevant content without repeating harmful material.
Do not post personal details or sensitive evidence. You do not need to engage
with someone who is harassing you.

Horus does not currently publish a dedicated private moderation contact. If a
report needs privacy, use GitHub's reporting tools rather than a public issue or
discussion. A private maintainer reporting channel should be established before
this policy is described as offering confidential project reporting. Security
vulnerabilities follow [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).

## Moderation

Maintainers may redirect off-topic content, ask participants to edit a comment,
remove harmful material, lock a thread, or restrict participation. Actions should
be proportionate to the behavior and its impact. Where safe and practical,
maintainers should explain the rule involved and allow correction.

A typical progression is a reminder or correction, a warning, a temporary
restriction, and a permanent restriction for severe or repeated misconduct.
Serious harassment, threats, or disclosure of private information may require
immediate protective action. Good-faith technical disagreement is not misconduct.

Consider available evidence and context fairly, minimize sharing of sensitive
reports, and avoid promises of confidentiality that cannot be kept. A maintainer
personally involved in a dispute should seek review from another available
maintainer where possible. A participant can request reconsideration through the
same safe reporting route, supplying new context without restarting the dispute.
No response deadline or particular staffing level is promised.

## Basis

This project policy follows the inclusive participation and proportionate
moderation principles of the
[Contributor Covenant](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct/)
and [GitHub Community Guidelines](https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/github-terms/github-community-guidelines).
